audit_findings.title: Current share denominator is paired with a pre-repurchase interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $49.722 million filed increase in first-half 2026 net interest expense versus first-half 2025, equal to 7.82% of the $636.2 million anchor OE; full-year adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: Also on December 8, 2025, the Company borrowed $1.35 billion under the Term Loan Facilities, the full amount available under the Term Loan Facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: the valuation uses the post-repurchase share count, while 2025 OE includes only a short period of interest on the December 2025 term loans. Because equity-level OE retains interest expense, the higher recurring net interest burden must be reflected in the anchor. The first-half increase is already large relative to anchor OE and is reasonably capable of materially reducing every scenario value.
audit_findings.action: Recast anchor OE using a full year of interest on the July 2026 debt balances, associated swaps and cash balances, apply the tax effect, and rerun all scenarios with the unchanged 66.705294 million diluted shares.

audit_findings.title: CBA contingent consideration may be absent from both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $760.396 million filed liability at July 3, 2026, equal to $11.40 per diluted share and 7.91% of base equity value; $37.126 million paid in first-half 2026 and $70-$80 million filed 2026 payment estimate
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to the CBA, the Company is required to make quarterly acquisition related sub-bottling payments to CCR on a continuing basis in exchange for the grant of exclusive rights to distribute, promote, market and sell the authorized brands of The Coca‑Cola Company and related products in certain distribution territories the Company acquired from CCR.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual payments and omission from the stated bridge are demonstrated; whether OE already deducts the cash payments is unresolved. Because the payments are financing cash flows, they will not enter ordinary operating cash flow automatically. If neither normalized payments nor the liability was deducted, the valuation materially overstates common-equity value. The liability and cash-payment scale are material, but they must not both be deducted.
audit_findings.action: Trace each OE year to confirm whether actual or normalized CBA sub-bottling payments were deducted. If absent, rerun using either a normalized after-tax OE deduction reflecting covered gross profit growth or a $760.396 million bridge deduction, but not both.

audit_findings.title: Deferred executive compensation is an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $217.1 million gross filed obligation, equal to $3.25 per diluted share and 2.26% of the $9.618 billion base equity value; disclosed deferred-compensation plan assets were $95.195 million at December 31, 2025
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company estimated obligations for its executive benefit plans to be $217.1 million, of which $40.6 million is expected to be paid in fiscal year 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but the incremental uncovered claim is not because designated assets support part of the obligation and OE may already capture compensation accruals. Even deducting the entire gross obligation with no asset offset would reduce base value by only $3.25 per share, leaving it well below the $189.33 market price and not changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Match each executive-plan liability to designated assets and reconcile cash settlements against OE accrual expense. Deduct only any uncovered past-service amount not already captured; no full rerun is necessary unless that reconciliation identifies additional obligations beyond the filed $217.1 million.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded postretirement benefits may be omitted from distributable cash flow
audit_findings.magnitude: $73.671 million filed obligation, equal to $1.10 per diluted share and 0.77% of base equity value; $4.373 million anticipated 2026 payment equals 0.69% of anchor OE
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had obligations related to its postretirement benefits plan of $73.7 million, of which $4.4 million is expected to be paid in fiscal year 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded obligation is demonstrated, while double-counting versus recognized benefit expense remains unresolved. Even a conservative bridge deduction of the entire obligation would reduce base value by about $1.10 per share and cannot close the $19.74 gap between the bull value and market price. The expected annual cash payment is also below 1% of anchor OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile benefit payments with service cost, interest cost and OE adjustments, then deduct only the portion not already recognized. Document the result without changing the conclusion unless new obligations materially exceed the filed amount.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capex must respect contractual operating floors
audit_findings.evidence: Under the CBA and the RMA, which authorize the Company to distribute and/or manufacture products of The Coca‑Cola Company, and pursuant to the Company’s distribution agreements with other beverage companies, the Company must satisfy various requirements, such as making minimum capital expenditures or maintaining certain performance rates.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of contractual minimum capital-spending requirements is demonstrated, but the supplied valuation contains no maintenance-capex schedule or contractual minimum amount. Filed total capex was $312.315 million in 2025, $147.354 million in first-half 2026, and approximately $300 million is expected for 2026; these figures show that capex is large relative to OE but do not identify the maintenance portion or establish an error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the CBA/RMA minimum-capex requirements and the valuation's annual maintenance-capex deductions; reconcile them to replacement needs and the filed 2025-2026 spending, then rerun if normalized maintenance capex is below the contractual or operating floor.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE may mix parent earnings with consolidated cash-flow components
audit_findings.mechanism: historical OE trend, growth selection and RONTA
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements include the accounts and the consolidated operations of the Company and its majority-owned subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The reported basis gaps indicate a historical consistency problem, but no dollar amounts are supplied to establish its valuation effect. The latest-year cap protects the $636.2 million anchor unless the corrected $1.135 billion trend falls by more than $498.8 million, or 43.95%. Nevertheless, corrections could still affect the selected growth scenarios and the 76.8% RONTA judgment, so materiality cannot be resolved from the record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2017-2020 net income, D&A, capex and adjustments on one ownership basis, quantify the NCI portion, recompute the historical trend and RONTA, and rerun only if the corrected evidence changes the anchor constraint or scenario-growth selection.
